div.head: II Cn 24.3
div.ab: And us ne þingð na riht, þæt ænig man agnian sceole, þær gewitnesse byð, ⁊ man gecnawan cann, þæt þær bregde byð; þæt nan man hit nah to geahnianne raþost þinga ær syx monðum, æfter ðam þe hit forstolen wæs.
And us ne ðincð na riht, þæt ænig man ahnian scule, ðær gewitnysse bið, [⁊ mann gecnawan cán, þæt þær brygde biþ]; þæt nan man hit nah to geahniannne raðost ðinga ær syx monðum, ðe hit forstolen wæs.

⁊ us ne þincþ nan riht, þæt ænig man agnian sceole, þær gewitnysse byð, ⁊ man gecnawan can, þæt þær bregde bið; þæt nan man hit nah to geagnianne raðost þinga ær six monðum, æfter þam þe hit stolen wæs.
Et nobis non uidetur rectum, ut aliquis propriare cogatur, ubi testimonium est et cognosci potest, quod ibi brede sit; et nemo id propriare debeat ante VI menses, postquam furatum est.
Nobis tamen iniustum uidetur, quod aliquis debeat sibi iurando uindicare, quod iuste suum est, ubi testes sunt, et saltem ante sex menses, postquam furto ablatum est quod quęrit.

Neque enim nobis rectum uidetur, ut quisquam sibi uendicare deprehensum debeat, ubi fideles testes sint, et animaduerti possit, quod subductum sit, ut quisquam, inquam, deprehensum sibi uendicare debeat, ad citissimum ante sex menses, postquam subductum fuit.
And us ne ðincð na riht þæt ænig man ahnian scule, ðær gewitnysse bið ⁊ man gec[n]awan cán, þæt þær brygde biþ; þæt nan man hit nah to geahnianne raðost ðinga ær syx monðum ðe hit forstolen wæs.

And us ne þingð na riht þæt ænig man agnian sceole þær gewitnesse byð, and man gecnawan cann þæt þær bregde byð; þæt nan man hit nah to geahnianne raþost þinga ær syx monðum, æfter ðam þe hit forstolen wæs.

Uns dünkt jedoch nicht richtig (kein Recht A), dass jemand [im Anefang verklagt, das Angeschlagene] als sein Eigen beschwören dürfe, da wo Zeugenschaft [für den Bestohlenen] vorhanden ist, und man erkennen kann, dass da Betrügerei [beim Besitzenden] vorwaltet: dass [also fortan] niemand es als sein Eigenthum erklären darf vor frühestens sechs Monaten, nachdem es gestohlen worden ist.

But it seems to us not right (no right, A) that anyone [sued by attachment] should be allowed to swear [the attached item] to be his own where there is witness [for the person robbed] and it can be recognised that there is fraud [on the possessor's part]: so that [henceforth] no one may claim it as his own until at the earliest six months after it was stolen.

But we regard it as unjust that anyone should claim ownership in a case where there is evidence by which it can be recognised that fraud is involved; so that no-one ought to claim ownership of it in less than six months at least from the time when it was stolen.

And it does not seem right to us that any man should make good his claim where there is witness and it can be shown that there has been fraud; so that no one ought to make good his claim until at least six months after it was stolen….

And it does not seem just to us that anyone should assert possession when there are witnesses and fraud can be proven; such being the case, no one should assert possession of anything less than six months at least from when it was stolen.
